tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

content.text:
The user wants me to ask questions to clarify their needs, then start "这两份数据集的合并优化" — merge/optimize the two datasets, targeting the **text-to-table** field, but with depth and special points, because current text-to-table is shallow. They want to deeply communicate to grasp requirements, then start the next upgrade.

So the deliverable this turn: a well-designed set of questions (not too many, high information), using `ask_user_question` perhaps, with options. The user explicitly says "请你问我一些问题核对我的需求" — so I should ask questions. The tool `ask_user_question` supports multiple questions with options, multi-select. That's ideal: ask 4-6 crisp questions, each with options, then after answers, plan.

But the user also says "然后开启这两份数据集的合并优化" — they want to proceed after Q&A. So this turn: ask questions, don't start building. Use `ask_user_question` with maybe 5 questions:

1. **合并的目标形态**：是把 R28 的单球题嵌入长文本（长文本里含多个单球事件），还是把 220 场的"整场表"作为顶层、单球作为证据层？Options:
   - A. 长文本为主 + 单球子问题（一个卷宗里多处需要裁定）
   - B. 单球为主 + 长文本作为干扰/上下文
   - C. 双层：整场表 + 逐球证据链，两个端点
   - D. 其他

2. **"深度"指什么**（multi-select）:
   - 多跳/跨文档证据整合
   - 版本化规则与冲突裁决
   - 计算/账目闭合（算术）
   - 反事实/证据必要性
   - 长上下文检索
   - 输出结构的复杂性（多表/多行）

Q: H4 人工上界 + 金标审计（60 题，2–3 人日）——最后一个硬阻断项。
A: H4 是 H1/H2 之后唯一不能自动化的部分：**需要两个真人**。其余工作我都能先做好。

## H4 实际包含两件事（同一批题，一次做完）

1. **金标审计**：两人独立查看 solver 金标，按四个维度（值、范围、规则版本、最小证明）判断对错 → 输出 H1（一致率）、H2（关键缺陷）。
2. **人类上界**：同两人**先盲推** 12 字段（不给金标），再与 solver 金标比对 → 得到人类逐字段准确率，以及“人类能否算账”的答案。

## 只有你能做的三件事

1. **找 2 个标注者**：懂板球计分，各投入约 1 天。至少 1 人**不参与 R28 构建**；如果两人都是作者，论文中必须写“非独立”，审稿人会降低评分。
2. **让他们阅读协议并做资格测试**：`ANNOTATION_PROTOCOL.md` 的 §1/§3，加上 20 道合成校准题，约 30 分钟；达到 ≥98% 才能进入正式样本。
3. **安排时间**：盲推 60 题约 6 小时/人，金标判定约 3 小时/人，仲裁约 2 小时（你或第三方）。

## 我可以先做好的

- 从 320 题抽 **60 题分层样本**：16 因子格 ×2 + 4 机制 ×3 剂量 + 16 个“字段锚点”（非零 BYE/LEG_BYE/PENALTY、各 dismissal），只用 published 臂。
- 绑定真实 build（`make_design.py resolve --strict`）、生成 public/gold bundle、泄漏筛查、生成离线 HTML 标注工具。
- 写打分脚本：两个 DERIVED 导出与 solver 金标比对，输出人类逐字段准确率，并和三模型面板、常数众数放在同一张表里。
- 产出 `H4_HUMAN_CEILING.md`：人类 vs llama

[短期上下文] 最近对话（共 5 轮）：
Q: H4 人工上界 + 金标审计（60 题，2–3 人日）——最后一个硬阻断项。
A: H4 是 H1/H2 之后唯一不能自动化的部分：**需要两个真人**。其余工作我都能先做好。

## H4 实际包含两件事（同一批题，一次做完）

1. **金标审计**：两人独立查看 solver 金标，按四个维度（值、范围、规则版本、最小证明）判断对错 → 输出 H1（一致率）、H2（关键缺陷）。
2. **人类上界**：同两人**先盲推** 12 字段（不给金标），再与 solver 金标比对 → 得到人类逐字段准确率，以及“人类能否算账”的答案。

## 只有你能做的三件事

1. **找 2 个标注者**：懂板球计分，各投入约 1 天。至少 1 人**不参与 R28 构建**；如果两人都是作者，论文中必须写“非独立”，审稿人会降低评分。
2. **让他们阅读协议并做资格测试**：`ANNOTATION_PROTOCOL.md` 的 §1/§3，加上 20 道合成校准题，约 30 分钟；达到 ≥98% 才能进入正式样本。
3. **安排时间**：盲推 60 题约 6 小时/人，金标判定约 3 小时/人，仲裁约 2 小时（你或第三方）。

## 我可以先做好的

- 从 320 题抽 **60 题分层样本**：16 因子格 ×2 + 4 机制 ×3 剂量 + 16 个“字段锚点”（非零 BYE/LEG_BYE/PENALTY、各 dismissal），只用 published 臂。
- 绑定真实 build（`make_design.py resolve --strict`）、生成 public/gold bundle、泄漏筛查、生成离线 HTML 标注工具。
- 写打分脚本：两个 DERIVED 导出与 solver 金标比对，输出人类逐字段准确率，并和三模型面板、常数众数放在同一张表里。
- 产出 `H4_HUMAN_CEILING.md`：人类 vs llama

- depth_axes: 版本化规则与冲突裁决、账目闭合、证据必要性/反事实、长上下文检索、表格结构复杂度 (5 selected!)

Now I need to produce the merge plan + first-round experiment design, within 1 week, 0 budget, solo human. They want "开启下一步的升级" — so give a concrete plan and perhaps start building. Given 1 week min viable, I should propose a 1-week scope that is honest: not a full 220-match rebuild; a **proof-of-depth slice** (e.g., 20-30 matches) that demonstrates the deep text-to-table task and gives first numbers.

Key design tensions:
- They selected 5 depth axes (all). With 1 week, can't do all. I need to prioritize: the **structural constraint** (table closure) + **version/conflict** + **evidence necessity** are the defining depth; long-context retrieval and table complexity are properties, not separate axes. I should tell them: 5 axes is too many for 1 week; pick 2 as *manipulated variables* (version conflict, closure) and treat the rest as fixed design properties. Be direct.

- Data: pure synthetic, 220 matches. Good: no license/new data.

- Task: long dossier (~65KB) → whole-match scorecard (multi-row table). But the 220 corpus's commentary is only 5.5KB, and R19's public instance is 65KB. The 65KB R19 is the "fragmented terminal" version with 14 decisive docs. The R28 single-ball is 1.3KB. To build "long dossier → whole scorecard" we need a match-level dossier that aggregates per-ball facts. Does the 220 corpus have ball-by-ball facts? Data card B1 says the 220 source is **innings-level aggregate only, no ball-by-ball**. That's a critical constraint! The R28 single-ball facts are template-injected, not from the 220 matches. So we cannot simply merge: the 220 corpus lacks per-delivery facts.

This is the key technical obstacle I must surface. Options:
1. **Synthesize the missing ball-by-ball layer**: generate a ball-by-ball sequence consistent with each match's innings-level scorecard (a constrained inverse problem: find a sequence of deliveries + extras + dismissals that sums to the scorecard). This is doable deterministically: we have the target table; generate a delivery sequence that closes to it. That's actually a great "depth" design: the model must reconstruct the table from a long commentary that narrates the balls; the gold table is the 220 scorecard; the ball-by-ball facts are generated to be consistent. But if we generate the commentary from the table, the table is trivially the source. The task's difficulty comes from evidence distribution/versions, not from the source.
2. **Use R28's single-ball facts as the atomic layer, and assemble matches**: take 9-12 R28 single-ball items and compose a "match" whose scorecard is the aggregation. But R28 items are independent balls from 64 scenes; composing them into an innings requires consistency (same batter/bowler/over). Could be done with the generator, but it's new data generation (~days).
3. **Use R19's 65KB per-match dossier**: it already has 14 targets and 14 decisive docs, amendment chains. The output is a 14-field record, not a whole scorecard table. Could we extend the output to a whole table? R19's private_gold is 5.8KB — likely 14 fields; not a full scorecard.
4. **Use the 220 match-level commentary as the long text, and define the table as the scorecard**, with depth added by: versioned rules (which scoring rule applies), amendments (retroactive corrections), and closure. The commentary would need to be rewritten to embed amendments/conflicts (the existing extracted system can regenerate commentary). This is feasible: the 220 matches already have scorecards and a generator; add amendment chains and conflict docs, then regenerate the long dossier. That's the "merge" path: R28's *mechanisms* (versioned rules, conflicts, certificates) applied to the 220 matches' *table* target, with the 220 commentary as the base long text.

So the merge = **220 match tables (the target) + R28 mechanism layer (versions/conflicts/evidence/certificates) + long dossier rendering**. The ball-by-ball detail is not required if the table is innings-level; the evidence is in the commentary (narrative) + amendment docs. Depth comes from:
- The table has cross-cell closure (runs = sum, extras = sum, bowling = runs conceded).
- Amendments/versions change cells retroactively.
- Evidence necessity: each cell has a minimal evidence set.
- Long context: 65KB dossier.

That's a coherent design that doesn't need ball-by-ball facts. The task: given a 65KB dossier (commentary + amendments + rule extracts + conflicting sources), output the final scorecard table (multi-row: batters, bowlers, extras, total). This is "deep text-to-table".

But the 220 commentary is only 5.5KB; to reach 65KB we need to add documents: rule extracts, amendment chains (1-14), conflicting sources, prior versions, scorecards of other matches as distractors. The R19 machinery does this at the 14-target level. We can adapt: per match, generate amendment chain for each table cell (or row), plus rule extracts, plus distractors. That's a generator job, maybe 2-4 days.

Within 1 week, the minimum viable proof:
- Take **20 matches** from the 220.
- For each, build a 30-60KB dossier: original commentary + N amendment docs + rule extracts + a few distractor docs.
- Gold: the amended final scorecard table (cells).
- Run 3 local models; score cell-level exact and **row/column closure**; measure "copy vs derive".
- Add a **version-conflict** condition: the same fact appears in two versions; only one is in force.
- Add an **evidence-necessity** check: delete one decisive doc; answer must change (countermodel).
- Human: only the author; so no human gold this week — but can do a **self-audit** of 20 items and disclose.

The key deliverable this week: a **20-match deep slice + eval harness + 3-model results**, enough to know if the task is real and hard, and to write the paper's method section.

But is generating 20 match dossiers feasible in 1 week? The 220 match tables + commentary exist. Amendments can be generated deterministically from the table: e.g., a "correction memo" that changes a batter's score, then a later memo that corrects the correction, with only the latest in force. The final table is computed by applying the chain. The commentary is the narrative; the amendments are the depth. That's a tractable generator: parse scorecard.md → table → inject amendments → render docs. The `src/parser.py` exists.

However, there's a catch: if the amendment memos directly state the corrected numbers, the task becomes "read the last memo" — shallow. To force derivation, the amendments should state *events* (e.g., "the 4th ball of over 12 was a no-ball, not a wide") not the final cell values; the model must recompute the table. That's deep. But the 220 scorecard is innings-level; can we map an event change to a cell change? Yes: change a delivery's type → change extras and bowler runs; change a batter's runs → change batter total and team total; etc. The generator can maintain the table and apply event-level amendments, then recompute.

This is a solid design: **event-level amendment chains** on top of the 220 tables. The model sees the narrative + amendments (events) and must output the final table. Depth = event→cell derivation + closure + version conflict + long context.

Feasibility in 1 week:
- Day 1-2: build the 20-match deep slice generator (parse scorecard, apply event amendments, render dossier, gold table).
- Day 3: eval harness (cell-level exact, row/col closure, record exact) + run 3 local models (20 × 3 = 60 calls).
- Day 4: add version-conflict arm (20 × 3 = 60 calls) and evidence-necessity check (delete one doc; 20 × 3?).
- Day 5: analysis + 1-page memo + decide go/no-go.

That's ambitious but plausible with my help; the user has 1 week. I should be honest: the 1-week scope is a **pilot**, not a full dataset.

Alternatively, a smaller MVP: 10 matches, 3 models, one arm. But 20 gives some stats.

Now, the response: the user wants "开启这两份数据集的合并优化" — they want me to start. I should:
1. State the plan (design + week schedule).
2. Surface the key obstacle: the 220 corpus has no ball-by-ball facts; so the merge must be at the **table-cell + event-amendment** level, not by injecting R28 single balls. This is important and honest.
3. Decide the 5 axes: pick 2 primary (version/conflict + closure), 2 secondary (evidence necessity, long-context), table complexity as a fixed property. Explain why 5 is too many for 1 week.
4. Propose the schema: how many rows/cols; the table format; the four conditions.
5. Start building: inspect one scorecard.md to see the table shape, then write the generator? That's a lot for one turn.

The user said "然后开启下一步的升级" — they expect action. I could start by inspecting the scorecard format and the extracted generator, then produce a concrete design doc + first generator skeleton. But a full generator is a multi-hour task; this turn can produce the **design + first working slice** (e.g., parse one match, inject one amendment, render one dossier). That would be a strong start.

However, I must be careful with the 1-week/minimal constraint and the user's solo-human constraint. The plan should include a **go/no-go gate**: if the 20-match slice shows models can solve it (cell exact >80%) or it's unsolvable (<20%), pivot.

Also, the human constraint: only the author. So for this week, no H4; the paper can't claim human validation. But the deep text-to-table paper is new; human audit can come later. I should note that.

Let me inspect:

Read one match's four files (5.5KB each = 22KB total, ~6k tokens). That's a lot but necessary to design. Maybe read scorecard.md and meta.json, skim commentary first 40 lines, and evidence_chain first 40 lines. Let me do that.

Then produce the design + start the generator? A generator needs careful work; perhaps this turn: design + data audit + a tiny prototype (parse table, count cells) to prove feasibility. Then next turn build.

{"content": """"Corpus audit for the deep text-to-table merge (220-match scorecard corpus).

Read-only. Counts table cells per match, evidence-chain levels, and text sizes.
Outputs DEEP_T2T/corpus_audit.json.

Run: python DEEP_T2T/audit_corpus.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

BASE = os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    "Self-cricket-clean_text_scorecard_v1_220_matches",
)
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "corpus_audit.json")


def md_tables(text: str) -> list[list[list[str]]]:
    tables, cur = [], []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.strip().startswith("|"):
            cur.append(line)
        elif cur:
            tables.append(cur)
            cur = []
    if cur:
        tables.append(cur)
    out = []
    for t in tables:
        rows = [[c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for ln in t]
        rows = [r for r in rows if not all(set(c) <= set("-: ") for c in r)]
        if rows:
            out.append(rows)
    return out


def table_kind(header: list[str]) -> str:
    h = " ".join(header).lower()
    if "field" in h and "value" in h:
        return "summary"
    if h.startswith("batter"):
        return "batting"
    if h.startswith("bowler"):
        return "bowling"
    if h.startswith("partnership"):
        return "partnership"
    if h.startswith("wkt"):
        return "fow"
    return "other"


def main() -> int:
    matches = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(BASE) if d.startswith("match_"))
    per_match = []
    totals = Counter()
    kinds = Counter()
    levels = Counter()
    text_bytes = Counter()
    for m in matches:
        d = os.path.join(BASE, m)
        sc_path = os.path.join(d, "scorecard.md")
        ev_path = os.path.join(d, "evidence_chain.md")
        cm_path = os.path.join(d, "commentary.txt")
        if not (os.path.exists(sc_path) and os.path.exists(ev_path)):
            continue
        sc = open(sc_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        ev = open(ev_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        cm = open(cm_path, encoding="utf-8").read() if os.path.exists(cm_path) else ""
        tables = md_tables(sc)
        cells = 0
        for t in tables:
            header, body = t[0], t[1:]
            kind = table_kind(header)
            kinds[kind] += 1
            n = len(body) * len(header)
            totals[kind] += n
            cells += n
        lv = Counter()
        for line in ev.splitlines():
            mm = re.match(r"\|\s*(L[123])\s*\|", line)
            if mm:
                lv[mm.group(1)] += 1
                levels[mm.group(1)] += 1
        text_bytes["scorecard"] += len(sc.encode("utf-8"))
        text_bytes["evidence"] += len(ev.encode("utf-8"))
        text_bytes["commentary"] += len(cm.encode("utf-8"))
        per_match.append(
            {
                "match": m,
                "tables": len(tables),
                "cells": cells,
                "batting_rows": sum(len(t) - 1 for t in tables if table_kind(t[0]) == "batting"),
                "bowling_rows": sum(len(t) - 1 for t in tables if table_kind(t[0]) == "bowling"),
                "evidence": {k: lv.get(k, 0) for k in ("L1", "L2", "L3")},
            }
        )

    n = len(per_match)
    summary = {
        "schema": "vett.deep_t2t.corpus_audit.v1",
        "n_matches": n,
        "cells_total": sum(p["cells"] for p in per_match),
        "cells_mean": round(sum(p["cells"] for p in per_match) / n, 1) if n else 0,
        "cells_by_kind": dict(totals),
        "tables_by_kind": dict(kinds),
        "evidence_rows": dict(levels),
        "evidence_share": {k: round(levels[k] / sum(levels.values()), 3) for k in ("L1", "L2", "L3")}
        if sum(levels.values())
        else {},
        "text_kb_mean": {k: round(v / n / 1024, 1) for k, v in text_bytes.items()} if n else {},
        "per_match_first5": per_match[:5],
    }
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"summary": summary, "per_match": per_match}, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Run: python DEEP_T2T/audit_corpus.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

BASE = os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    "Self-cricket-clean_text_scorecard_v1_220_matches",
)
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "corpus_audit.json")


def md_tables(text: str) -> list[list[list[str]]]:
    tables, cur = [], []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.strip().startswith("|"):
            cur.append(line)
        elif cur:
            tables.append(cur)
            cur = []
    if cur:
        tables.append(cur)
    out = []
    for t in tables:
        rows = [[c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for ln in t]
        rows = [r for r in rows if not all(set(c) <= set("-: ") for c in r)]
        if rows:
            out.append(rows)
    return out


def table_kind(header: list[str]) -> str:
    h = " ".join(header).lower()
    if "field" in h and "value" in h:
        return "summary"
    if h.startswith("batter"):
        return "batting"
    if h.startswith("bowler"):
        return "bowling"
    if h.startswith("partnership"):
        return "partnership"
    if h.startswith("wkt"):
        return "fow"
    return "other"


def main() -> int:
    matches = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(BASE) if d.startswith("match_"))
    per_match = []
    totals = Counter()
    kinds = Counter()
    levels = Counter()
    text_bytes = Counter()
    for m in matches:
        d = os.path.join(BASE, m)
        sc_path = os.path.join(d, "scorecard.md")
        ev_path = os.path.join(d, "evidence_chain.md")
        cm_path = os.path.join(d, "commentary.txt")
        if not (os.path.exists(sc_path) and os.path.exists(ev_path)):
            continue
        sc = open(sc_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        ev = open(ev_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        cm = open(cm_path, encoding="utf-8").read() if os.path.exists(cm_path) else ""
        tables = md_tables(sc)
        cells = 0
        for t in tables:
            header, body = t[0], t[1:]
            kind = table_kind(header)
            kinds[kind] += 1
            n = len(body) * len(header)
            totals[kind] += n
            cells += n
        lv = Counter()
        for line in ev.splitlines():
            mm = re.match(r"\|\s*(L[123])\s*\|", line)
            if mm:
                lv[mm.group(1)] += 1
                levels[mm.group(1)] += 1
        text_bytes["scorecard"] += len(sc.encode("utf-8"))
        text_bytes["evidence"] += len(ev.encode("utf-8"))
        text_bytes["commentary"] += len(cm.encode("utf-8"))
        per_match.append(
            {
                "match": m,
                "tables": len(tables),
                "cells": cells,
                "batting_rows": sum(len(t) - 1 for t in tables if table_kind(t[0]) == "batting"),
                "bowling_rows": sum(len(t) - 1 for t in tables if table_kind(t[0]) == "bowling"),
                "evidence": {k: lv.get(k, 0) for k in ("L1", "L2", "L3")},
            }
        )

    n = len(per_match)
    summary = {
        "schema": "vett.deep_t2t.corpus_audit.v1",
        "n_matches": n,
        "cells_total": sum(p["cells"] for p in per_match),
        "cells_mean": round(sum(p["cells"] for p in per_match) / n, 1) if n else 0,
        "cells_by_kind": dict(totals),
        "tables_by_kind": dict(kinds),
        "evidence_rows": dict(levels),
        "evidence_share": {k: round(levels[k] / sum(levels.values()), 3) for k in ("L1", "L2", "L3")}
        if sum(levels.values())
        else {},
        "text_kb_mean": {k: round(v / n / 1024, 1) for k, v in text_bytes.items()} if n else {},
        "per_match_first5": per_match[:5],
    }
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"summary": summary, "per_match": per_match}, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Excellent audit numbers:
- 220 matches, **98,572 cells**, mean 448 cells/match.
- Evidence chain: L1 32.1%, L2 40.9%, L3 27.0% — so **68% of evidence-chain targets are L2/L3** (derivation/synthesis), not direct extraction. This is a strong argument that the corpus is not shallow, if we target L2/L3 cells.
- Text sizes: scorecard 5.2KB, evidence 2.5KB, commentary 6.4KB.

Key design implication: the full scorecard is 448 cells — too large for a 640-token output. We need a **compact target table** (e.g., 20-30 cells) per item, selected from L2/L3 targets. But the user wants whole scorecard. For a 1-week MVP, choose a **subset of tables**: innings summary (16 cells) + FOW (15) + top-3 batting/bowling? Still ~80 cells.

Output token estimate: 80 cells × ~6 tokens = 480 tokens, plus structure ~100. Fits 2K. Prompt: 6.4KB commentary (~1.8K tokens) + amendments (~5KB) + rules (~2KB) ≈ 9-10K tokens > 8K. Hmm.

Need to keep prompt ≤ ~6K tokens: commentary 6.4KB (~1.8K) + amendments 8KB (~2.2K) + rules 4KB (~1.1K) + template 1K ≈ 6.1K. Output 2K → 8.1K, tight. Reduce output table to ~40 cells (300 tokens) → fits.

Alternatively, increase num_ctx to 12K or 16K for the pilot. 3070 8GB: qwen 7B Q4 5.1GB at 8K; 16K KV maybe +0.7GB → 5.8GB, fits; llama 8B ~6.5GB, fits; gemma 9B Q4_0 5.4GB + KV ~1GB → 6.4GB, maybe. So 12K is feasible; 16K risky for gemma. For the pilot, use 12K for qwen/llama, 8K for gemma? Inconsistent. Better: cap prompt at ~7K tokens (28KB) and output 1K; use 8K.

The design should target **~25KB dossier** (~6.5K tokens), output **compact table ~40 cells** (~400 tokens). That fits 8K with margin.

But the user's choice "整场记分卡" — the compact table is a subset. I'll explain: full 448-cell table is impossible at 8K; the pilot targets 40 **derived** cells (the L2/L3 ones), which is the deep part; the full table is the scale-up with a 32K/cloud model.

Now the plan:

**Task name**: DeepT2T / "VETT-DeepTable".
**Input**: a ~25KB dossier per match: original commentary (narrative) + N event-level amendment memos + 2 rule extracts (one superseded) + 2 distractors.
**Output**: a compact scorecard table with ~40 cells, of which:
- 25% directly stated (L1)
- 50% require closure (L2)
- 25% require cross-doc/version reasoning (L3-ish)
**Conditions**:
- C0 baseline: commentary only (no amendments, no conflicts).
- C1 + amendments (event corrections, only latest in force).
- C2 + version conflict (rule extract v1 superseded by v2; some cells depend on which version).
- C3 + delete-one-evidence (necessity check; gold changes or becomes underdetermined).
**Models**: qwen2.5:7b, llama3.1:8b, gemma2:9b. 20 matches × 4 conditions × 3 = 240 calls; ~30-60 min each model? Prompt 25KB, output 400 tokens; maybe 10-15s/call → 240 × 12s = 48 min. Fine.

**Metrics**:
- cell exact (per cell type)
- full-table exact
- **closure violation rate** (sum rows ≠ total, extras sum ≠ total extras, bowling runs ≠ total − byes/leg-byes, wickets sum ≠ 10)
- **copy rate** (cell equals a directly stated number — measures shallow copying)
- **derivation rate** (L2 cells correct)
- **version sensitivity** (C2 vs C1: cells that change when the rule version changes)
- **evidence necessity** (C3: flip rate)

**Gate**:
- If cell exact >80% in C0 → too easy; increase depth.
- If full-table exact 0% and closure violations >50% → task is real; proceed.
- If no model can produce parseable table → output format too hard; use JSON schema / grammar.

**Week schedule**:
- Day 1-2: generator for 20 matches (parse scorecard, select 40 cells, inject amendments, render dossier, gold).
- Day 3: eval harness + 3 models × 4 conditions.
- Day 4: analysis + reliability (repeat 10 items).
- Day 5: 1-page memo + go/no-go + paper outline.

**Human**: only author → no H4 this week; disclose; the pilot is a feasibility study, not the final paper.

But the user said "1 周 / 最小可行". This schedule is ambitious but doable with my help. The generator is the hard part: event-level amendments that change cells. Need to design amendment types:
- Batter runs correction: "the 3rd ball of over 12 was scored 2, not 1" → batter total +1, team total +1, SR changes.
- Extra type correction: "the 5th ball was a wide, not a no-ball" → wides +1, no-balls −1, bowler runs unchanged? Actually both charge 1 to bowler? No-ball and wide both 1 extra, but no-ball may have runs off bat. Complex.
- Dismissal change: "the batter was caught, not bowled" → dismissal text changes, bowler wicket stays.
- Over count correction: "the 18th over had 5 legal balls, not 6" → overs total changes.
- Amendment chain: memo 1 changes, memo 2 supersedes memo 1, memo 3 voids memo 2? Only latest in force.
- Rule version: "Law 22.9 (2026) after Wide, dismissal possible only under X; the 2025 extract says Y" — one cell (dismissal validity) depends on version.

The gold table is recomputed by applying the event changes to the parsed table. This requires a **table model** with dependencies (runs, balls, SR, extras, total, bowling figures, FOW). That's a mini-solver. Doable but 1-2 days.

Alternative simpler amendment: amendments directly modify **cells** but the memo states the event, and the gold is recomputed by a small rule engine. Still need the engine.

For MVP, could restrict to **runs and extras** corrections (affect batter R, team total, extras breakdown, SR, RR, bowling R) — 6 fields; no dismissal/over changes. That's simpler. Version conflict affects one cell (wide dismissal validity) — can be a separate small arm.

## 0. 一句话

把 220 场的“整场表”从**抄写任务**改造成**约束满足任务**：

## 1. 审计事实（`corpus_audit.json`）

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---:|
| 场数 | 220 |
| 表格 cell 总数 | **98,572** |
| 每场平均 cell | **448.1** |
| batting / partnership / bowling / FOW / summary | 33,908 / 24,563 / 20,992 / 9,837 / 9,260 |
| evidence chain L1 / L2 / L3 | 32.1% / **40.9%** / **27.0%** |
| 文本均值 | commentary 6.4 KB、scorecard 5.2 KB、evidence 2.5 KB |

**关键读法**：语料本身不浅——68% 的证据目标是 L2/L3（闭合/综合），
浅的是“当前任务只问 L1 直取”。深度不是再造数据，是**把评分对象移到 L2/L3 的 cell 上**。

## 2. 三个硬约束（设计必须绕开）

1. **220 源只有局级聚合，没有逐球事实**（数据卡 B1）。不能在 220 场上直接注入 R28 单球；

2. **本地 8K 上下文**：卷宗 ≤ ~25KB（约 6.5K token），输出 ≤ ~1K token。

## 3. 任务定义

**输入（~25KB 卷宗）**
- 解说原文（6.4KB，叙事）
- 3–5 条**事件级**修订备忘：写“某球发生了什么”，不写最终数字
- 2 份规则摘录（v2025 / v2026，其中一份被取代）
- 2 份干扰文档（另一场的数据）

- 每局 top-3 bowlers ×（O, M, R, W）（24）
- FOW chain（10 + 5）（15）
（约 79 cells；实际进入评分的 ~40 个是 L2/L3 依赖 cell）

**cell 构成**
- 25% L1：直取（抄对即可）
- 50% L2：闭合（行和、列和、extras、bowling 账、wickets 和、overs 和）
- 25% L3：版本/跨文档（哪条规则生效、哪份修订在force、干扰文档是否被误用）

| 条件 | 操纵 | 回答 |

| **C0** | 只有解说 | 浅层基线：模型能抄多少 |

- `derivation_rate`（L2 cell 正确率）

[短期上下文] 最近对话（共 5 轮）：
Q: H4 人工上界 + 金标审计（60 题，2–3 人日）——最后一个硬阻断项。
A: H4 是 H1/H2 之后唯一不能自动化的部分：**需要两个真人**。其余工作我都能先做好。

## H4 实际包含两件事（同一批题，一次做完）

1. **金标审计**：两人独立查看 solver 金标，按四个维度（值、范围、规则版本、最小证明）判断对错 → 输出 H1（一致率）、H2（关键缺陷）。
2. **人类上界**：同两人**先盲推** 12 字段（不给金标），再与 solver 金标比对 → 得到人类逐字段准确率，以及“人类能否算账”的答案。

## 只有你能做的三件事

1. **找 2 个标注者**：懂板球计分，各投入约 1 天。至少 1 人**不参与 R28 构建**；如果两人都是作者，论文中必须写“非独立”，审稿人会降低评分。
2. **让他们阅读协议并做资格测试**：`ANNOTATION_PROTOCOL.md` 的 §1/§3，加上 20 道合成校准题，约 30 分钟；达到 ≥98% 才能进入正式样本。
3. **安排时间**：盲推 60 题约 6 小时/人，金标判定约 3 小时/人，仲裁约 2 小时（你或第三方）。

## 我可以先做好的

- 从 320 题抽 **60 题分层样本**：16 因子格 ×2 + 4 机制 ×3 剂量 + 16 个“字段锚点”（非零 BYE/LEG_BYE/PENALTY、各 dismissal），只用 published 臂。
- 绑定真实 build（`make_design.py resolve --strict`）、生成 public/gold bundle、泄漏筛查、生成离线 HTML 标注工具。
- 写打分脚本：两个 DERIVED 导出与 solver 金标比对，输出人类逐字段准确率，并和三模型面板、常数众数放在同一张表里。
- 产出 `H4_HUMAN_CEILING.md`：人类 vs llama

Q: 列举一下现在已有的成果
A: # 现有成果清单（2026-11-13）

## 一、数据与仪器（可交付）

| 项 | 数字 / 状态 | 位置 |
|---|---|---|
| R28 数据集 | **360 题**（320 发布 + 40 held-out），64 场，版本 `v0.37` | [dataset_r28](VETT_R28_DIFFICULTY_20261112/03_build/dataset_r28) |
| 构建确定性 | 12/12 验收，重跑逐字节一致；`build_index` `dd6de16a…` | 同上 |

| 12 字段 / 9 信息字段 | 常数字段已非零：BYE 96、LEG_BYE 78、PENALTY 153 | 数据卡 |
| 记录互异 | **320/320 = 1.0**；可达记录下界 **761**；合法 dismissal 记录 **11** | `record_space_probe.json` |
| 双渲染 | published vs control，facts/record **320/320 逐字节相同** | t6/t8 |
| 证书 | **320/320** 可重推；`rule_path` 只含承载算子；solver 重推 **100%** | t6/t8 |
| 装饰性规则 span | **488/1546 = 31.6%** 从未承载；**360/360** 题至少含 1 条 | t5 |

| 发布件 | 数据卡、held-out 协议 + 评分器、CC BY 4.0 / MIT、`reproduce.py --che

Q: 那怎么办，我感觉我之前的长文本不是没用了吗
A: 并非没用——它只是从“主数据集”降级成另外两样东西：**R28 的外部效度**，以及**第二篇论文**。你现在把这两件事混在一起看，才会觉得它被废了。

## 你手上的长文本有三层，而且都有产出

| 层 | 是什么 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| 220 场原始 | `commentary.txt` → `scorecard.md`，每场 4 文件 | 880 文件，完整 |
| R19 审计版 | 6 实例，**14 个目标、14 份决定性文档、1–14 层修订链**；22 种公开捷径攻击大多 **0/84**，最高 6/84（7.14%） | 机器 PASS；单实例 `public_instance.json` **65 KB** |
| R26.18 长文本 pilot | 5 场 × 5 题，125K token 批次，GLM-5.3-Flash | **5/5 完整**，已出数 |

## 它已经跑出的硬结果

R26.18：字段宏准确率 **66.33%**，信息字段 **55.11%** vs 常数先验 52.89%（skill **仅 4.72pp**），**整记录 exact 0/25**，span F1 45.2%、edge F1 29.9%。

把它和 R28 放在一起：

| | 长文本（R26.18，5 场/25 题，125K token） | 短文本（R28，320 题，1.3K token） |
|---|---|---|
| 字段准确率 | 66.33% | 59.56% |
| 相对先验 | +4.72pp | +4.53pp |
| **整记录 exact** | **0/25** | **0.78%** |

**同一个模式在两个格式、两个模型、两个尺度上复现了：字段级只比先验高一点点，联合 exact 接近 0。** 

Q: 现在请你问我一些问题核对我的需求，然后开启这两份数据集的合并优化，我针对的目前领域还是为文本转表格方向，但是内容和深度和侧重点可以有不一样的特殊点，毕竟现在都只是针对于浅层的文本转表格，我需要深度，需要可以有说服力的，所以我需要我们深度沟通，把握需求，然后开启下一步的升级
A: 合并之前，先确定六件事。我的初始判断先放在这里供你反驳：

> **正确的合并方式是把 R28 的单球裁定作为整场记分卡的“隐藏中间步骤”，而不是把 320 题塞进 220 场。** 一场对应一份 65KB 卷宗，输出多行记分卡；每个 cell 都必须由证据链推导出来，不能照抄。深度来自三件事：表格的结构约束（行和等于列和、extras 闭合）、证据链长度，以及版本冲突；把文本单纯变长并不能带来深度。

请回答下面六个问题；回答后我会直接给出合并方案与第一轮实验设计。

content.text:
The user says "继续" — continue. They've answered the six questions. I've already:
- Written `DEEP_T2T/PLAN_V1.md`
- Written `DEEP_T2T/audit_corpus.py` and run it, got 220 matches / 98,572 cells / 448 per match / L1 32.1% L2 40.9% L3 27.0%.

Now "继续" means: proceed with the merge upgrade. The next step per my plan is D1: build the 20-match builder: parse scorecard → select cells → inject amendments → render dossier + gold. That's a substantial script. I should build it now.

But first, I need to design the amendment mechanics carefully, and I need to understand the commentary text to know how the narrative states numbers (so amendments can be event-level and gold recomputed). Let me read a commentary sample (5.5KB) to see style. Then design the builder.

Also, key question: what exactly are the ~40 scored cells? The plan says summary 16 + top-3 batters 24 + top-3 bowlers 24 + FOW 15 = 79. For MVP, maybe 40: 16 summary + 12 top-3 batters (3 fields: R,B,4s?) + 12 bowlers (O,R,W?) + FOW? Need to decide.

Let me think about the builder mechanics:

1. Parse `scorecard.md` into structured tables:
   - match info (venue, toss, result, POM, umpires)
   - innings 1/2: summary fields, batting rows, bowling rows, partnerships, FOW.

2. Select cells to score:
   - Innings summary: total runs, wickets, overs, extras, byes, leg-byes, no-balls, wides, run rate, max partnership (2 innings × 10 = 20).
   - Top-3 batters by runs per innings: name, R, B, 4s, 6s (2 × 3 × 5 = 30).
   - Top-3 bowlers by wickets then economy: name, O, M, R, W (2 × 3 × 4 = 24).
   - Top scorer / best bowling (2 × 2 = 4).
   - Result / winner (2).
   Total ~80. For output budget, 80 cells ≈ 400-600 tokens. OK.

   But "top-3" requires ranking, which is a derivation itself (sort by runs). That's good depth. But if the ranking is wrong, all cells mismatch; scoring should be by cell content keyed by player name, not row position. Better: gold table includes all 11 batters? 11 × 5 = 55 per innings — too big. Alternatively, score a fixed subset: the **top-3 by runs** (gold knows), and the model must output those 3; if it picks wrong players, those rows are wrong. That's fine.

   Simpler and more robust: score the **innings summary (20 cells)** + **top-3 batters' R/B/4s/6s (30)** + **top-3 bowlers' O/R/W (18)** + **FOW chain?** FOW requires 10 numbers per innings; too much. Skip FOW for MVP.

   Total 68 cells. Output ~400 tokens.

3. Amendments: event-level changes that alter cells. Need a small "table model" to recompute gold. Options:
   - **Runs amendment**: "the 3rd ball of over 12 was hit for 2, not 1" → batter total +1, team total +1, batter SR changes, bowler runs +1, bowling econ changes, partnership runs +1, FOW after that point +1 for subsequent wickets, max partnership may change.
     That cascades to many cells; recomputing FOW/partnerships is complex.
   - **Extras amendment**: "the 4th ball of over 8 was a wide, not a leg-bye" → leg-byes −1, wides +1, total unchanged, bowler runs unchanged? (both charge to bowler? leg-byes are not charged to bowler; wides are charged). So bowler runs +1, extras breakdown changes, econ changes. Complex but tractable.
   - **Dismissal amendment**: "the batter at 4 was caught, not lbw" → dismissal text, bowler wicket unchanged, FOW end text changes. Summary cells unchanged.
   - **Overs amendment**: "the 18th over had 5 legal balls" → overs total changes, RR changes.

   For MVP, restrict amendments to **summary-level effects that are easy to recompute**:
   - Change a batter's runs by ±1/2: affects batter R, team total, extras? No, runs off bat; affects total, batter R, SR, bowler R, econ, partnership runs, FOW after. Cascade is complex but can be recomputed from a **ball-by-ball model**... which we don't have.
   
   Hmm. Without ball-by-ball, cascade recomputation is hard. Alternative: amendments that affect **only one row/cell**:
   - "The catcher for the 3rd wicket was X, not Y" → dismissal text only.
   - "The Player of the Match was X, not Y" → one cell.
   - "The venue was X" → one cell.
   These are shallow (no derivation).
   
   To force derivation, amendments should change a **component** whose **total is constrained**: e.g., "byes were 4, not 2" → byes +2, total +2, bowling runs −2, econ changes, RR changes. Recompute: total, extras, byes, bowling R (total − byes − leg-byes), econ, RR. That's a closed-form cascade, no ball-by-ball needed! 
   - Wides/no-balls: affect total, extras, bowling runs (charged), econ, RR.
   - Leg-byes: affect total, extras, bowling runs (not charged).
   - Batter runs: affects total, batter R, SR, bowling R, econ, RR; but also batting sum = total − extras, so consistent.
   - A batter's balls faced: affects SR only.

   So amendments at the **component level** (byes, leg-byes, wides, no-balls, a batter's R) can be recomputed via closure formulas, without ball-by-ball. 

   Example: "Correction memo: the first innings contained 4 byes, not 2." Gold recompute:
   - byes = 4
   - extras = old extras + 2 = 23
   - total = batting runs + extras = 144 + 2 = 146? Wait, if byes increase by 2, total increases by 2 (runs are runs). But the original total 144 = batting 123 + extras 21. If byes +2, total 146, batting unchanged. Bowling runs = total − byes − leg-byes = 146 − 4 − 3 = 139 (unchanged!). Interesting: bowling runs unchanged. RR changes because total changes.
   - So closure gives: total 146, extras 23, byes 4, bowling runs 139, RR 146/35.3.
   
   That's a clean derivation: the model must recompute total and extras from the amendment, not just copy.

   Another: "the fourth batter's score was 51, not 49." Then batting sum +2, total +2, extras unchanged, bowling runs +2, econ changes, batter R/SR changes, partnership runs change (the partnership containing that batter), max partnership may change. Partnership recompute is harder but can be approximated: the partnership involving the batter at the time. Hmm.

   For MVP, restrict to **extras components** and **total-level** corrections, plus **version conflict** on a rule that affects one cell (e.g., whether a wide can be stumped → dismissal valid/invalid). That's enough to demonstrate closure + version.

   But the user wants "版本化规则与冲突裁决" and "账目闭合" and "证据必要性" and "表格结构". Extras amendments give closure. Version conflict gives rule choice. Evidence necessity: delete the amendment memo → the cell reverts to old value; the answer must change. That's easy to implement: C3 removes the memo; gold is the pre-amendment table. Wait, "delete one decisive doc" means the answer becomes underdetermined, not "reverts". If the memo is the only source of the correction, deleting it makes the amended cell unknowable → model should abstain or output old value. For scoring, "answer changes" is the flip. The gold for C3 is the pre-amendment table (the commentary states old value); if the model outputs old value, it's "consistent with available evidence" but wrong relative to the true amended table. The necessity test is: does removing the doc change the model's answer? That's a paired comparison, not accuracy. Good.

   Version conflict: two rule extracts:
   - v2025: "A ball that passes the bat and hits the stumps is a bowled dismissal." 
   - v2026: "If the ball is a no-ball, the batter cannot be bowled." 
   A case where a no-ball + hit stumps → under v2025 bowled; under v2026 not out (no-ball). The table's dismissal cell depends on the version. 1: Eastgate Sports Oval in Harbor City gave Brookfield XI and Stoneford XI one of those awkward mid-range contests where the target never looks huge on paper, yet every wicket and every quiet over keeps adding weight until the chase starts to feel much tighter than the score alone suggests. Brookfield won the toss, chose to field, and the first innings immediately justified the call in patches, because Stoneford never really found a clean top-order rhythm even though Aaron Holt opened with the sort of sharp little burst that can briefly disguise deeper problems. Holt’s 17 from 12 had real intent, two boundaries and a clean strike over the rope, but it was also too brief to become a platform, and when Lucas Shaw drew the chance to Nathan Frost, the innings was already starting to tilt toward Brookfield’s bowlers. Connor Vale tried to give the reply a more settled shape, Dylan Marsh gave him a small busy phase, and for a while Stoneford had just enough movement to avoid looking trapped, yet Ryan Cross kept cutting away the attempted repair. Marsh went first, then Connor followed after a patient but limited 15, and when Tyler Quinn was removed without scoring, Stoneford had slipped to 48 for 4 and the innings had lost almost all of its early confidence. Ethan Drake became the one batter who gave Stoneford a real spine. He did not rescue the innings with one reckless burst; he rebuilt it in pieces, first stopping the immediate slide, then giving Logan Pierce enough time to form the largest stand of the innings. Their 45-run partnership was the first passage where Brookfield had to work through overs rather than simply collect wickets, though even that recovery was not clean enough to fully transfer pressure back onto the fielding side. | 层 | 是什么 | 状态 |

> **正确的合并方式是把 R28 的单球裁定作为整场记分卡的“隐藏中间步骤”，而不是把 320 题塞进 220 场。** 一场对应一份 65KB 卷宗，输出多行记分卡；每个 cell 都必须由证据链推导出来，不能照抄。深度来自三件事：表格的结构约束（行和等于列和、extras 闭合）、证据链长度，以及版本冲突；把文本单纯变长并不能带来深度。

深度轴 — 你说的“深度”，最想压哪两根轴？（可多选，最多 3 项）
回答：版本化规则与冲突裁决, 账目闭合（算术）, 证据必要性/反事实, 长上下文检索, 表格结构复杂度

数据来源 — 升级后的数据来源怎么定？
回答：纯合成，延续 220 场（推荐）

发表口径 — 这次升级主要按哪个口径设计？
回答：ACL/EMNLP Resource & Evaluation（推荐）

可投入资源 — 这次升级你能投入多少时间与预算？
回答：1 周 / 最小可行

人工审计 — 这次能安排几个真人做金标/人类上界？
回答：只有我 1 人

The user said "继续". I already wrote PLAN_V1.md and ran the audit. Now I should continue with D1: build the 20-match builder.

But the user's "继续" came after the answers block, and the current context shows the plan+audit were produced. So the next step is the builder. I need to actually write `DEEP_T2T/build_deep20.py` and run it on 20 matches.

This is a substantial script. Let me design it carefully.

Key data:
- `match_XXXX/scorecard.md` with tables:
  - match info: Field/Value (Venue, Toss, Result, POM, Umpires, Referee)
  - innings summary: Field/Value per innings (Total, Total Extras, Byes, Leg Byes, No Balls, Wides, Run Rate, Max Partnership)
  - batting: Batter | Dismissal | R | B | 4s | 6s | SR
  - bowling: Bowler | O | M | R | W | Econ | Wd | Nb
  - partnerships, FOW.
- `commentary.txt`: one long line (5-6KB).
- `evidence_chain.md`.

Goal for D1:
- Parse 20 matches.
- Build compact gold: innings summary (7 fields ×2), top-3 batters (5 fields ×3 ×2), top-3 bowlers (4 fields ×3 ×2), result, POM.
- Inject 3-4 amendments at extras/batter level.
- Recompute gold via closure.
- Render dossier: commentary + amendments + rules (v2025/v2026) + distractor + question.
- Write JSON per match.

I need to be careful with parsing:
- The innings section starts with `## <Team> - <total> (<overs>)`.
- Tables under it.
- `Total` field value "144/10 (35.3 Overs)" → parse runs, wickets, overs.
- `Total Extras` 21, `Byes` 2, `Leg Byes` 3, `No Balls` 1, `Wides` 15, `Run Rate` 4.06, `Max Partnership` 45.
- Batting rows: `Aaron Holt (c)` etc.; dismissal text; R,B,4s,6s,SR.
- Bowling rows: `Ryan Cross`, O `7`, M `1`, R `25`, W `2`, Econ, Wd, Nb.

Top-3 by R (batters), by W then Econ (bowlers).

Amendments (deterministic, seeded by match id for reproducibility):
Types:
1. `byes_up`: +K byes (K=1 or 2). Effects: byes += K; extras += K; total += K; RR = total/overs; bowling_runs = total - byes - leg_byes (unchanged? total +K, byes +K → unchanged). So bowling runs unchanged; good closure test (total/extras/RR change).
2. `leg_byes_to_byes`: move K from leg_byes to byes. Effects: byes += K; leg_byes -= K; extras unchanged; total unchanged; bowling_runs = total - byes - leg_byes: byes +K, leg_byes -K → unchanged. Only composition changes. Hmm weak.
3. `bat_plus`: batter R += K; batting_runs += K; total += K; extras unchanged; bowling_runs = total - byes - leg_byes += K; RR changes; batter SR changes (SR = R/B*100); top-3 order may change.
4. `wide_to_noball`: wides -= K; no_balls += K; extras unchanged; total unchanged; bowling_runs unchanged (both charged). Composition only.

For MVP, use combination: 1 `byes_up` + 1 `bat_plus` + 1 `wide_to_noball` per match. The gold recompute:
- batting_runs_old = total_old - extras_old.
- Apply bat_plus to a specific batter: batter.r += K; batting_runs += K; total += K.
- Apply byes_up: byes += K; extras += K; total += K.
- wide_to_noball: wides -= K; no_balls += K (extras unchanged, total unchanged).
- Recompute extras = byes + leg_byes + no_balls + wides.
- total = batting_runs + extras.
- RR = total / overs_decimal.
- For the batter's SR = R/B*100.
- Bowling runs: total - byes - leg_byes (team-level). Per-bowler R unchanged (we don't amend a bowler).
- Top-3 batters re-rank after the batter change; if the amended batter moves into top-3, the top-3 set changes — that's a derivation. But then the gold top-3 rows change, and the model must output the new top-3. Good.
- Top-3 bowlers unchanged.

But wait: if `bat_plus` changes a batter's R, the batting sum changes and total changes; but the **commentary** may state the old total and old batter score. The model must update. Good.

Version conflict: add a rule doc pair:
- v2025: "Byes are charged against the bowler when the ball is not a no-ball or wide." (false-ish; byes are NOT charged)
- v2026: "Byes and leg byes are not charged against the bowler." (true)
This affects `bowling_runs` computation. If the model uses v2025, bowling_runs = total - leg_byes only (byes charged) → different. The scored cell `bowling_runs` (team-level) would differ. But this is a rule-text-only difference, no event; it's a clean version conflict. Gold uses v2026. The model must select the in-force version (v2026 supersedes v2025 per a "playing conditions" memo).
- Also a dismissal rule: "A batter caught off a no-ball is not out (v2026) vs out (v2025)". Needs an event; skip for MVP.

So the table includes a `bowling_runs` cell for each innings:
- innings 1: 144 − 2 − 3 = 139 (matches evidence_chain: "144 - byes 2 - leg byes 3 = 139").
- innings 2: 145 − 0 − 2 = 143.
This is a great L2 cell, and the version conflict directly affects it. 

Scored cells:
- `innings[0].total_runs`, `total_wickets`, `overs`, `extras`, `byes`, `leg_byes`, `no_balls`, `wides`, `run_rate`, `bowling_runs` (10)
- same for innings 2 (10)
- `result`, `pom` (2)
- top-3 batters: 3 × (R, B, 4s, 6s) ×2 = 24
- top-3 bowlers: 3 × (O, R, W) ×2 = 18
Total 64 cells. Output ~350 tokens.

Gold table schema:
```json
{
  "match_id": "match_0001",
  "innings": [
    {"team": "...", "total_runs": 146, "wickets": 10, "overs": "35.3",
     "extras": 23, "byes": 4, "leg_byes": 3, "no_balls": 1, "wides": 15,
     "run_rate": 4.12, "bowling_runs": 139,
     "top_batters": [...], "top_bowlers": [...]}
  ],
  "result": "...", "pom": "Nolan Hart"
}
```

Dossier:
- `docs/00_match_metadata.md`: venue/toss/teams (from match info).
- `docs/01_commentary.md`: commentary.
- `docs/02_amendments.md`: 3 memos, each event-level:
  - M1: "In the Stoneford XI innings, the two extras recorded as leg byes on the 12th ball were in fact byes." → byes +2, leg_byes −2 (composition; no total change). Hmm I wanted byes_up. Let me make M1: "the scorers under-recorded byes by 2 in the first innings; two additional byes were signalled." → byes +2, extras +2, total +2. 
  - M2: "Ethan Drake's score of 49 was corrected to 51: two runs were credited to the wrong batter." → batter +2, batting +2, total +2.
  - M3: "The delivery recorded as a wide in the second innings was a no-ball; no runs were scored off it." → wides −1, no_balls +1 (composition).
  These are plausible.
- `docs/03_rules_v2025.md`, `docs/04_rules_v2026.md`: extracts, with a header "superseded" on v2025.
- `docs/05_distractor.md`: commentary from another match (different teams).
- `question.md`: schema + "use only documents in this dossier; apply the in-force 2026 conditions; output JSON table".

Condition variants:
- C0: no amendments, no version conflict, no distractor → just commentary + question.
- C1: + amendments.
- C2: + version conflict (v2025 superseded vs v2026).
- C3: C1 but remove M2 (the batter amendment) → necessity test.

The builder can emit dossier per condition, with gold per condition:
- C0 gold = original table (bowling_runs with v2026 rule? C0 has no rule docs, so bowling_runs not asked? To keep the schema constant, C0 should also ask for bowling_runs; but without rules, the model may not know byes aren't charged. That's fine—it's prior knowledge. Or C0 excludes bowling_runs. Better: keep schema constant, C0 has no rule docs; the model uses its own knowledge.)
- C1 gold = amended table (with v2026 rule for bowling_runs).
- C2 gold = same as C1 but rule versions differ; the correct is v2026.
- C3 gold = original table (M2 removed) but M1/M3 applied.

This is implementable.

But wait: the commentary is 6.4KB and may explicitly state the old values; the amendments must be the only source of new values. The dossier should not include the scorecard table. Good.

Version conflict details:
- v2025 extract: "Law 17.3 (2025): byes are charged to the bowler's analysis." (This is wrong in real cricket, but it's a fictional rule version; fine.)
- v2026 extract: "Law 17.3 (2026): byes and leg byes are not charged to any bowler."
- A "playing conditions" memo: "The 2026 extracts supersede the 2025 extracts for this match."
The model must use v2026 → bowling_runs = total − byes − leg_byes. Under v2025 → total − leg_byes. The gold cell differs.

This is a clean version-conflict experiment on one cell, without needing event changes.

Now, is `bowling_runs` derivable per innings? In the scorecard, bowling figures sum to it (evidence_chain L2). If the model sums the bowlers' R, it gets the same number without the rule. That's a shortcut: the rule version doesn't matter if you sum the bowling table—but the bowling table isn't given! The dossier excludes the scorecard. The commentary may mention individual figures; the model would have to parse them. Hmm, the commentary likely states some figures. The shortcut may exist. But the cell is still a derivation from either rule or sum; both are valid. For version sensitivity, the rule changes the *formula*, but if the model computes from the commentary's figures, it may match v2026 anyway. The version conflict may not bind.

To make it bind, the commentary should not give the full bowling figures; it's narrative, likely gives some. The model can't sum what it doesn't have. Then it must use the rule + total. Under v2025, it would subtract only leg_byes. So the version test works if the model applies the rule.

But honestly, a model may just output the original 139 from the commentary (if stated). Then C2 vs C1 no difference. The version sensitivity might be low. We'll see.

For MVP, it's okay; the experiment will show.

Now, writing the builder is a lot. Let me scope it to ~250 lines:
- parse functions
- select 20 matches (e.g., first 20 with 11+11 batting rows and both innings)
- amendments
- gold recompute
- render
- write

I need to handle markdown table parsing (already have in audit).
Parsing innings: split scorecard by `## ` headings; the first `## Team - total (overs)`; then tables. The summary table is the first `Field/Value` after the heading; batting table header starts with Batter; bowling with Bowler.
Match info: tables before the first `## `.

Parsing `Total`: "144/10 (35.3 Overs)" → regex `(\d+)/(\d+) \(([\d.]+) Overs\)`.

Top-3 batters: sort by R desc, then B asc? Use R desc, name.
Top-3 bowlers: sort by W desc, then R asc, then name.

Amendments:
- A1 byes +2 in innings 0 (first innings).
- A2 batter +2 in innings 0: pick the top scorer (Ethan Drake 49 → 51). Then top-3 re-rank; he likely stays #1.
  But if top scorer +2, batting sum +2, total +2. Gold: total 146, extras 23 (after A1), batting 125? Original batting 123, +2 = 125; extras 23; total 148? Wait: original total 144 = batting 123 + extras 21. A1 byes +2 → extras 23, total 146. A2 batter +2 → batting 125, total 148. Yes. Bowling runs = 148 − 4 − 3 = 141 (original 139 +2). Good cascade.
- A3 wide→no-ball in innings 1: wides 7→6, no_balls 1→2; extras unchanged 10; total unchanged 145; bowling runs unchanged 143.

Gold C1:
- innings 0: total 148, wickets 10, overs 35.3, extras 23, byes 4, leg_byes 3, no_balls 1, wides 15, RR 148/35.5 = 4.17, bowling_runs 141.
  Overs 35.3 = 35 + 3/6 = 35.5. RR = 148/35.5 = 4.169.
- innings 1: unchanged except wides 6, no_balls 2; total 145; extras 10; RR 4.35; bowling_runs 143.
- top-3 batters innings 0: Ethan Drake 51 (B 62, 4s 6, 6s 1), Aaron Holt 17, Connor Vale 15. Re-rank: still same top 3.
- top-3 bowlers: innings 0: Nolan Hart 8-2-18-3, Caleb Stone 10-1-43-3, Ryan Cross 7-1-25-2? Sort by W desc: Hart 3, Stone 3, Cross 2, Shaw 1, Rowe 1 → top3 Hart, Stone, Cross. innings 1: Logan Pierce 10-2-27-3, Gavin Reed 8.2-1-38-1, Carter Hayes 8-1-34-1.

Scoring by cell: keyed by innings + field + player.

This is doable. The builder can write a `gold.json` with cells as a dict, and a `dossier.json` with documents. The eval harness later compares model JSON to gold cells.

Output JSON schema for the model:

Now, writing the builder. I'll write it to `DEEP_T2T/build_deep20.py`, run it, and inspect one dossier.

But this is a lot of code. Let me be efficient and write a clean ~300-line script. I'll test on 1 match first (`--limit 1`) then 20.

A: 并非没用——它只是从“主数据集”降级成另外两样东西：**R28 的外部效度**，以及**第二篇论文**。你现在把这两件事混在一起看，才会觉得它被废了。

| 层 | 是什么 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| 220 场原始 | `commentary.txt` → `scorecard.md`，每场 4 文件 | 880 文件，完整 |
| R19 审计版 | 6 实例，**14 个目标、14 份决定性文档、1–14 层修订链**；22 种公开捷径攻击大多 **0/84**，最高 6/84（7.14%） | 机器 PASS；单实例 `public_instance.json` **65 KB** |
| R26.18 长文本 pilot | 5 场 × 5 题，125K token 批次，GLM-5.3-Flash | **5/5 完整**，已出数 |

R26.18：字段宏准确率 **66.33%**，信息字段 **55.11%** vs 常数先验 52.89%（skill **仅 4.72pp**），**整记录 exact 0/25**，span F1 45.2%、edge F1 29.9%。

| | 长文本（R26.18，5 场/25 题，125K token） | 短文本（R28，320 题，1.3K token） |

| 相对先验 | +4.72pp | +4.53pp |
| **整记录 exact** | **0/25** | **0.78%** |

**同一个模式在两个格式、两个模型、两个尺度上复现了：字段级只比先验高一点点，联合 exact 接近 0。**
